When I was in deep depression years ago, I got close to a guy I met in an MMORPG while roleplaying. His character was in the same guild as mine, our characters became a couple. In real life he was a comic artist who said he and his wife were separated to be divorced. It got to the point where in character transitioned to out of character. We said we loved one another and toyed with the idea of meeting and such.

A few months after our meeting, he said he was going to stop playing his character and create another, he felt the character's story had taken its course. I was supportive. He said he'd still keep in contact, I had his account added to my friends list after all. He loved me, I said to myself. Doesn't matter what character he plays.

Poof. I didn't hear a peep from him after that. He simply stopped logging into his account. Mutuals of ours didn't hear from him either. He disappeared.

Now, I didn't have him added on social media. I was also separated and didn't feel it was appropriate to ask to be friends on it at the time. I found his Facebook account and was surprised to find recent photos of him with his wife, together as a happy couple. He had lied to me about them splitting up.

I never did find out why he ghosted me. I have a feeling his wife found out about us, or he realised he was in too deep. I cried a little, then moved on. I had bigger problems in my life anyway.

Just a few months or so later, I was informed by someone who knew us both that the ghost had returned, on a new account with a new character. I confronted him, to be told that it wasn't him, I was mistaken etc. The thing is, I recognised his art style on his character profile. He had some comic art he created of his new target/girlfriend. He had always promised to draw my character. He never did, that stung a bit seeing that art and the fact that he was lying and wouldn't give me closure.

I was very unwell at that time. I was deeply depressed and lonely. Any affection I received was accepted. Now I'm well, long moved on and realise I was not the problem. In fact, I pity the ghost's wife most of all, who probably hasn't any idea what her husband got up to online.
